content.text: Introduction
Web server is an intermediary between the client and the server. It retrieves content for each request and transmits it to the network.
Its main task is to handle multiple requests simultaneously. Properly configuring server files reduces load and improves site performance.

blocks.text: Web servers process files written in PHP, Python, JavaScript and others.

content.text: Simply put: a web server connects server and client.
Web servers
Today there are many web servers. The most popular are Apache and Nginx.
We won’t compare them in detail, but will cover their basics and configuration.

blocks.text: Nginx and Apache are software installed on the server.

content.text: Apache
When a client visits a page, Apache returns requested files (text, images, etc.) using HTTP/HTTPS.

blocks.text: Apache is modular and highly customizable.

content.text: Modules allow enabling/disabling security, caching, URL editing, authentication and more.
Configurations can be set with the .htaccess file.

blocks.text: Typically .htaccess is placed in the site root, but it can also be placed in subdirectories.

content.text: Nginx
Nginx is a web server and mail proxy, released in 2004. It is efficient for static websites and as a reverse proxy for dynamic ones.

blocks.text: Nginx is fast, reliable and not overloaded with features.

items: Serving requests, index files, file lists
Proxying without caching, load balancing, fault tolerance

content.text: Apache or Nginx?
Nginx was created to solve the c10k problem (10,000 concurrent connections).
Apache uses a threaded structure and may slow under high traffic. Nginx uses an event-driven architecture with a master process and workers.

blocks.text: Nginx distributes requests efficiently across workers, improving scalability.
Apache may be easier for small sites thanks to modules and simpler setup.

content.text: Web server setup
Configuration files are usually customized per site or framework, but some general settings apply to all.
Key modules: URL editing and caching, both important for SEO and performance.

blocks.text: Text compression (gzip) reduces file size and improves speed.
Basic setup includes custom error pages and removing .html/.php extensions.

content.text: Apache: .htaccess
All Apache add-ons are written in .htaccess, placed in site root.

blocks.text: It must be named exactly .htaccess, not my.htaccess.

content.text: Nginx: .conf
Nginx configs are in .conf files with flexible naming (e.g. cache-ng.conf).
